responsibility: Provides rustc’s per-compilation session layer: it defines and wires together the compiler’s central `Session` state in `session.rs`, the long-lived parsing state in `parse.rs`, and the crate root in `lib.rs` that re-exports the main session-facing APIs and establishes crate-wide hashing support. It owns the compiler’s configuration and option system through `config.rs` and `options.rs`, including the session configuration model, command-line parsing and dependency-tracked options, with `config` also supplying the canonical `-Z on-broken-pipe` mode constants used to interpret that setting consistently. It manages how the session finds inputs and outputs by implementing sysroot and library discovery in `filesearch.rs`, representing and parsing library search paths in `search_paths.rs`, and computing crate names, crate types, output filenames, and output-path validation in `output.rs`. It supplies the metadata and external-crate access side of a session via `cstore.rs`, which defines the abstract crate-store interface and shared metadata types for external crates, dependencies, sources, exported items, and native libraries. It also centralizes session diagnostics in `errors.rs`, declaring the structured errors used for configuration, target, linker, feature-gate, crate-name, and literal-parsing reporting. For compiler bookkeeping and debugging support, it tracks incremental codegen-unit reuse expectations and outcomes in `cgu_reuse_tracker.rs`, gathers code size, layout, and vtable statistics in `code_stats.rs`, and provides shared helpers in `utils.rs` for timing, native-library option handling, path canonicalization, ICE-report context, and Cargo detection. Together, these modules make `rustc_session` the crate that models, configures, validates, and supports the full compiler session environment that the rest of rustc relies on during a single crate compilation.
